en: Oṃ. Salutations again and again to the glorious Jagannātha.
This prayer,
which is always attended by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, vidyādharas, and uragas, possesses a splendor equal to ten million beautiful suns. (1)
One should meditate upon the divine Nārāyaṇa, the bestower of the fruits of the four aims of life.
Victory to you, Kṛṣṇa, Lord of the World! Victory to you, Supreme Leader of all! 2.
Victory to you, whose lotus feet are worshipped by the entire world; salutations be unto you! || 3 ||
Yudhiṣṭhira said: He by whose grace everything exists, he who is devoted solely to Viṣṇu, he who is the Ordainer and the Disposer, and he who is the supreme Truth—[to him I bow]. (1)
His illusory net, consisting of the three worlds with all their moving and non-moving beings, merely causes mortals to wander like those deceived by a mirage.
I bow with love for the world to the names and to the Lord of the World;
please tell me now that which was spoken by Bṛhatī.
Bhīṣma said:
O Yudhiṣṭhira, O mighty-armed one, listen as I recount the pure and auspicious names of the Lord of the World. (1)
By whose illusory power (māyā) this entire world, including all things moving and stationary, is pervaded;
and by whose grace, having created Brahmā, he protects him at all times.
Indeed, Brahmā and the other guardians of the ten directions are utterly deluded by his illusory power (māyā),
for the descent of his activities extends throughout the entire realm of the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa).
Compassion or affection for all beings is found everywhere in that Lord of the World, who is omnipresent and adorned with truth and righteousness. || 4 ||
O sinless one, I shall tell you thousands of your names.
Now, the Thousand-Name Hymn (Sahasranāmastotra) of Śrī Jagannātha.
Now, the application (viniyoga):
for this Mātṛkā mantra, Vedavyāsa is the seer (ṛṣi), and Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ).
The deity is Śrī Jagannātha; the application (viniyoga) is for the recitation of the Thousand Names for the sake of pleasing the Blessed Lord Śrī Jagannātha.
The meditation (dhyāna):
On the Blue Mountain, in the center of a conch, upon a hundred-petaled lotus, seated on a jeweled lion-throne,
adorned with all ornaments, possessing the luster of a fresh rain-cloud, joined by his elder brother,
and accompanied on Bhadrā’s left side by one who holds a discus— He who is worshipped by Brahmā, Rudra, and Indra.
I remember the Lord, the essence of the Vedas, who dwells in the Brahma-wood, surrounded by his own people.
The Blessed Lord said:
I am the four-armed Lord of the World, adorned with the Kaustubha gem upon my neck;
I am Padmanābha, whose womb is the Vedas, and whose eyes are the moon and the sun. || 1 ||
Jagannātha, Lord of the world, Sovereign of the Blue Mountain, the Supreme Hari; Friend of the distressed, Ocean of mercy, Compassionate One, Protector of humanity. || 2 ||
He who has conch-like arms, who holds the discus in his hand, whose navel is like a lotus, the best among men;
the protector of the worlds, the all-pervading, the pervader of all, the Lord of the gods. || 3 ||
The king of the world, the king of the gods, Śakra, the sovereign, the lord of the earth, the lord of the master of the Blue Mountain, Ananta, and Puruṣottama. || 4 ||
Tārkṣya, Udhyāya, Kalpataru, Vimalāprītivardhana, Balabhadra, Vāsudeva, Mādhava, and Madhusūdana. || 5 ||
The enemy of the Daityas, the lotus-eyed one, the wearer of the forest garland, the lover of strength;
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, of the Vṛṣṇi lineage, the enemy of Mura, Kṛṣṇa Keśava.
Śrī Rāma is existence-consciousness-bliss, Govinda, the Supreme Lord;
he is Viṣṇu, the Victorious, Mahāviṣṇu, the All-powerful, and Maheśvara.
The creator of the world, the Lord of the universe, the great creator of great renown;
the great seer, the teacher Kapila, the one who moves through the worlds, the god Hari.
The Self, the protector of living beings, the hero, the guardian of the world, the one who is not alone, the beloved of mine, the expounder of Brahman, and the Great Lord—[these are my names]. (9)
He has two arms, four arms, a hundred arms, and a thousand;
with eyes as broad as lotus petals, he is the supreme Hari, the inner essence of the lotus.
The lotus-handed one, the protector of the gods, the enemy of the Daityas, the destroyer of the Daityas; he who possesses four forms, four arms, and is served by the four-faced one (Brahmā). || 11 ||
He who holds a lotus in his hand, whose hand bears the discus, who holds a conch in his hand, and who wields the mace;
he who dwells in the great Vaikuṇṭha and who is forever the source of delight to Lakṣmī. 12.
Viśvanātha, the giver of joy, the one who brings pleasure to all the gods;
he who pervades the universe, whose form is wood, and whose eyes are the moon and the sun. || 13 ||
The discovery of the hidden Gaṅgā, the increaser of devotion to Tulasī, Jagadīśa, Śrīnivāsa, Śrīpati, and the elder brother of Śrī (Viṣṇu). 14.
The source of Sarasvatī, the foundation, Śrīvatsa, the treasure-house of fortune and compassion, Prajāpati, the lord of Bhṛgu, Bhārgava, and Nīlasundara. || 15 ||

Hari, the Lord who is the source of the universe, whose form consists of the qualities of *yogamāyā*, is the Sun; he is the rescuer from dissolution and, in the beginning, the protector of the world. (16)
Pervaded by compassion, lotus-handed, formless, and the refuge of the world;
lotus-navelled, shapeless, untainted, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). || 17 ||
The source of compassion, pervading the world, the bestower of prosperity, adorned with a conch shell;
as deep as ten million oceans, he is forever the giver of delight to the deities.
He is the Lord of the Gods, the Lord of Beings, the observer of celibacy, and the destroyer of cities;
he is the embodiment of space and wind, the embodiment of Brahman, and he who dwells within the waters.
He is Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the protector of vision, the supreme bestower of immortality; he is filled with supreme bliss, the meritorious god, and the ultimate refuge. || 20 ||
The wealthy one, the giver of wealth, the womb of wealth, the Great Lord;
the noose-handed one, the life of all beings, the protector of the entire cycle of existence. || 21 ||
The creator of the gods, the creator of Brahmā, the most excellent, the protector of Brahmā;
the Lord of the world, the preceptor of the gods, the pervader of the universe, and the conqueror of the senses. || 22 ||
He is the great form, the universal form, the one of great intelligence, and supreme valor;
he moves for the sake of the meaning of all seeds, and is the eternal seer and lord of the Vedas.
He is the life-force of all living beings, the lord of the earth, and the lord of the Maruts;
he is the mind, the intellect, and the ego, and the destroyer of desire, anger, and the like.
Kāmadeva, Kāmapāla, Kāmāṅga, Kāmavallabha; destroyer of enemies, ocean of compassion, merciful one, supreme lord. || 25 ||
He is the protector of the gods, the mother of the gods, the brother, the kinsman, the father, and the friend;
he is the child, the old man, the form of the body, the architect of the universe, the strong, and the weak. || 26 ||
He who possesses manifold forms, who is ever truthful, who is the refuge of the virtuous;
he who is the Brahman of the world, the Great Brahman, the Gross Brahman, and the Lord of the gods.
Pervading the world, ever-observant of right conduct, the lord of all beings and the king;
the guardian of the fortress, the master of the field, the lord of delight, and the leader of Rati. || 28 ||
The powerful one who moves with universal strength, the giver of strength, the dwarf Bali;
he whose smile is gentle, the autumnal moon, the supreme, the protector of the beyond. || 29 ||
He begins with the letter 'a' and ends with the letter 'ma', with the letter 'u' in the middle, maintaining his own essential nature;
he abides in praise, is the drinker of Soma, and is the maker of the utterances Svāhā and Svadhā.
The Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, Narasiṃha, Vāmana, Paraśurāma of great heroism, and Rāma, the son of Daśaratha. || 31 ||
The supreme delight of Devakī, the Man-lion, the protector of men;
he who wears a forest garland, the sustainer of the body, the one adorned with a lotus garland, the ornament of all. || 32 ||
He is the wearer of jasmine and garlands, always fond of the *jāti* and *yūthī* flowers;
he is the great-grandfather, the grandfather, the Brahmin, and the lover of Brahmins.
The King of Kalpas, the Lord of Birds, the Sovereign of Gods, the Beloved of the Gods;
the Supreme Self, the Strength of kings, the Auspicious One, the Source of All Auspiciousness. (34)
Possessing all powers, he is the sustainer of bodies and the bestower of strength upon kings;
he is the purifier and the protector of various birds and winged creatures. (35)
He wanders in Vṛndāvana and sports in eternal abodes;
he is the protector of the sacred field, the human being, the world itself, and the guardian of worldly existence. || 36 ||
He is sattva, rajas, tamas, intellect, and even the supreme ego;
he is space, fire, the sun, the moon, the earth, and the mountain that supports the earth.
Free from anxiety, absorbed in yogic sleep, compassionate, and the sustainer of the body;
the thousand-headed Śrī Viṣṇu is eternal, victorious, and without abode.
He is the creator, the destroyer, and the sustainer; the protector of true initiation and other vows;
lotus-eyed, self-existent, dark-hued, and fond of the forest. || 39 ||
He is the wish-fulfilling tree, the supreme among trees; he is Hari himself, the maker of the Kalpas;
he is the preceptor of the gods, possessing the form of all deities, and is worthy of salutation.
He who follows the conduct of the Vedas and Agamas, who is accessible to Kṛṣṇa, whose glory is self-manifested, Nārāyaṇa, the supreme lord of men and of the worlds. 41.
He is the Supreme Self of all living beings, the supreme Yama worshipped by the world, the abode of all creatures, the imperceptible, the dweller within all, and the refuge of the moving. || 42 ||
The daughter of Bhagiratha is his mind and intellect; Bhava (Shiva) stands as his death;
he is fond of worldly existence and is ever delighted, being the eternal protector of the world.
The god who assumes various colors, adorned with various flowers, the banner of joy, the embodiment of Brahman, the dweller on the mountain, the lord of the Gaṇas. || 44 ||
The wielder of illusion, the bearer of color, the lord of yogis, the bearer of fortune, Hari;
the great light, the one of great heroism, the powerful, and the source of strength. || 45 ||
The creator of beings, the source of existence, the god, the practitioner of celibacy, the lord of the gods;
Sarasvatī, the teacher of the gods, the god of the gods, the sovereign of the gods. || 46 ||
Rudra, who bears eight forms, is the embodiment of will, supreme valor,
the lord of great serpents, one of meritorious deeds, and a practitioner of austerity.
The protector of the day and the protector of the distressed, the divine lion and the maker of light;
the non-eater and the eater with [all], the consumer of the oblation, both the supreme and the subordinate.
Hari is the giver of mantras, the giver of knowledge, and the giver of all; he possesses supreme prosperity, the supreme dharma, and is saluted by all dharmas. || 49 ||
The embodiment of forgiveness, the embodiment of compassion, the giver of truth, and the protector of truth;
the enemy of Kaṃsa, the slayer of Keśin, and the destroyer of the wicked. || 50 ||
He is the one who brings joy to the Pāṇḍavas, the supreme protector of others, the sustainer of the world, the creator of the world, and the guardian of the cowherds and their calves. || 51 ||
The eternal Great Brahmā, the bestower of fruits upon those who perform actions, the supreme, the highest bliss, the ultimate prosperity, the Supreme Lord. || 52 ||
He is the refuge of all worlds, the upholder of all scriptures;
he is Dharmakīrti, the Great Dharma, whose very soul is Dharma, and the kinsman of Dharma.
The creator of the mind, possessed of great intelligence, the bestower of great majesty;
the Great Form of the worlds Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ, the formidable one of terrible prowess. || 54 ||

The God whose nature is the essence of what is wholesome, whose form is the path, higher than the highest; whose appearance is the universe, who contains the universe within him, who intoxicates the gods, and the Lord of the Suras. || 55 ||
The Lord of the world, the all-pervading, the Lord of existence, the protector of existence;
he who is worthy of being seen, the knower of the four Vedas, the one of auspicious limbs, and the witness of the worlds. || 56 ||
He is dark-complexioned and of peaceful form, perfectly tranquil and the most excellent among the clever;
he is the delight of the Sāman, the delight of the Ṛc, and the beloved of the Yajus and Atharvan.
Śyāmacandra, Caturmūrti, Caturbāhu, Caturgati, Mahājyotis, Mahāmūrti, Mahādhāman, Maheśvara. || 58 ||
Agasti is the giver of boons and the grandfather of all the gods;
he is the one who brings joy to Prahlāda and the savior of Dhruva’s pride.
Adorned with a beautiful body, the giver, the bestower of devotion to the virtuous, he is the syllable Om, the Supreme Brahman, the supportless Hari. 60.
He is the true goal, the supreme swan, the individual soul, and the leader of living beings;
he is conceived by the mind, the captor of the heart, the delightful one, and the bearer of the bow.
The Brāhmaṇa is the goal and the lord of the senses born of Brahman;
he is the Virāj, the lord of the gods, manifested from the three quarters above.
The supreme beyond the supreme is the highest quarter, seated upon a lotus with his throne in the lotus;
he is the object of various doubts, yet he is fully established in the knowledge of reality.
He is the omniscient one, the kinsman of the world, and the creator of the mind-born;
the Brahmin was born from his mouth, and the king was born from his vehicle.
The Vaiśya arose from his thighs, and the Śūdra from his feet; he is eternal and non-eternal, the knower, the proud one, the giver of color, the giver of all, and adorned by all.
He is free from doubt regarding the letters that have no beginning, situated above various karmas;
he is free from doubt regarding the pure and other qualities, possesses a body of Brahman, and has a smiling face.
The enemy of Śambara, the lord of the Vedas, the performer of good deeds, the increaser of courage, the bestower of everything upon all beings, and the one who pervades the universe. || 67 ||
Seeking the welfare of all beings and devoted to the well-being of all living creatures,
he always assumes a body and is eternally present as a young brahmin student.
He is the destroyer of all karma, the bestower of knowledge, and whose nature is compassion; he is the giver of the perfection of merit, as well as the creator and the destroyer.

He is the eternal dweller on the Blue Mountain (Nīlādri), he whose face is bowed in reverence, and he who is the destroyer of cities (Puraṃdara); he is the divine Nara and Nārāyaṇa, stainless and free from all affliction.
Brahmā, Śambhu, the best of gods, the conch-handed one, Balarāma, Arjuna, the creator of the world, the long-lived one, Govinda, and the beloved of the cowherds. || 71 ||
The god of gods, the Great Brahmā, the Great King, the Great Refuge;
the Infinite One, the Lord of Beings, and the Source of infinite beings. || 72 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī and enemy of Mura, who holds a flute in his hand, is the refuge of the oceans, the mountains, and likewise the Gandharvas. (73)
Abiding in the world, pervading the world, the source of all worldly existence;
he whose womb is filled with jewels, whose hands hold jewels, and who is the husband of the daughter of the ocean-mine.
He is the protector of Kandarpa and the grandfather of Kāmadeva;
his splendor is like ten million suns, and he is as cool as ten million moons.
Possessing the loveliness of ten million Cupids, the embodiment of desire, and of great austerity;
he dwells in the city of Mathurā, yet is Dvārika, the lord of Dvārakā. (76)
He is the lord of the spring season, Mādhava, who always bestows joy; he is the kinsman of Śyāma, dark as a rain cloud, with a luster equal to a dense, water-laden cloud.
He dwells for infinite eons, he is the witness of the eons, and he is the creator of the eons;
he is the Lord of Truth, the practitioner of truth, the speaker of truth, and is eternally established.
He who possesses four forms and four arms, the Lord of the four ages, Bhava;
Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, the end of the age, Balabhadra, Bala, and the Mighty One.
The Lord Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is the master of the Śālagrāma stone;
he is Prāṇa, Apāna, Samāna, as well as Udāna and Vyāna. (80)
He is fivefold in nature, the essence of the five elements, and the protector of those who have come for refuge;
whatever is seen in the world, all that is the Lord of the Universe.

The Lord of the World, the Great Brahman; salutations to You, the Lord of the World! The Lord of the World, the Great Brahman; salutations to You, the Lord of the World! The Lord of the World, the Great Brahman; salutations to You, the Lord of the World!
Thus ends the *Śrī Jagannātha Sahasranāma Stotra*.
Now begins the majesty of the Thousand Names of Śrī Jagannātha:
If this hymn is recited with these thousand names,
or if a person causes it to be read, or even listens to it— || 1 ||
By means of a sacrifice performed with a hundred thousand [offerings], one attains that merit which resides in all sacred fords (tīrthas) and especially in the Vedas. || 2 ||
A person quickly obtains that merit multiplied ten millionfold by [reciting] the meritorious and fruitful names of the Lord of the World. (3)
One seeking knowledge obtains knowledge; one seeking yoga attains yoga;
one seeking a daughter obtains a daughter; and one seeking victory obtains victory. || 4 ||
One who desires wealth obtains wealth; one who desires a son obtains a son.
Through the employment of this [rite], it always grants victory to kṣatriyas in battle. || 5 ||
It shall be the universal dharma for Vaiśyas, and it causes happiness to increase for Śūdras;
for those who recite it constantly, it bestows knowledge as well as its fruit.
That man never encounters slander nor suffering;
having attained the fruit of all happiness, that man shall become long-lived.
Listen, O mighty-armed King, to the majesty of the Lord of the Universe, by the mere remembrance of whom one is liberated from all sins. (8)
Whoever, being ever pure, recites the names of Jagannātha, the Lord of the World,
the sin arising from the Kali age perishes for him at that very moment.
Thus ends the "Thousand-Name Hymn of Śrī Jagannātha" in the Śrī Brahmapurāṇa, within the dialogue between Bhīṣma and Yudhiṣṭhira.
